---
title: "Testing a Design by Simulating From a DAG"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(dagitty)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Goal

Use a DAG to decide what to adjust for, then **check that decision by simulation**: generate data where we know the true effect, fit models with different adjustment sets, and plot which ones recover the truth.

# The design

Question: what is the effect of exercise on blood pressure?

- **Age** affects both exercise and blood pressure (a confounder).
- **Clinic visit** is caused by both exercise and blood pressure (a collider).

```{r}
dag <- dagitty("dag {
  Age -> Exercise
  Age -> BloodPressure
  Exercise -> BloodPressure
  Exercise -> ClinicVisit
  BloodPressure -> ClinicVisit
}")

coordinates(dag) <- list(
  x = c(Age = 0, Exercise = 1, BloodPressure = 3, ClinicVisit = 2),
  y = c(Age = 0, Exercise = 1, BloodPressure = 1, ClinicVisit = 2)
)

plot(dag)

adjustmentSets(dag, exposure = "Exercise", outcome = "BloodPressure")
```

dagitty says to adjust for `Age` and nothing else.

# Simulate data with a known effect

The true effect of one unit of exercise on blood pressure is **−2**.

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
true_effect <- -2

simulate_once <- function(n = 500) {
  age <- rnorm(n, 50, 10)
  exercise <- 10 - 0.1 * age + rnorm(n)
  blood_pressure <- 100 + 0.8 * age + true_effect * exercise + rnorm(n, sd = 5)
  clinic_visit <- exercise + 0.3 * blood_pressure + rnorm(n)
  tibble(age, exercise, blood_pressure, clinic_visit)
}

estimate <- function(data) {
  tibble(
    model = c("No adjustment", "Age (the DAG's set)", "Age + clinic visit (collider)"),
    estimate = c(
      coef(lm(blood_pressure ~ exercise, data))[["exercise"]],
      coef(lm(blood_pressure ~ exercise + age, data))[["exercise"]],
      coef(lm(blood_pressure ~ exercise + age + clinic_visit, data))[["exercise"]]
    )
  )
}

results <- bind_rows(lapply(1:500, function(i) estimate(simulate_once())))
```

# Plot which design recovers the truth

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
results |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = rev(unique(model)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = model)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", color = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = true_effect, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = true_effect, y = 3.45, label = "True effect", hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Only the DAG's adjustment set recovers the true effect",
    subtitle = "Estimated effect of exercise on blood pressure across 500 simulated datasets",
    x = "Estimated effect (mm Hg per unit of exercise)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

# Takeaways

- Leaving out the confounder (age) biases the estimate.
- Adjusting for a collider (clinic visit) biases it again, even with age included.
- A DAG states your assumptions; a simulation plus one plot shows what they imply. Change an arrow, re-run, and see whether your conclusion survives.
